newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia hit by four-hour railway strike.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia hit by four-hour railway strike.

text.p: Slovenian railway workers launched a four-hour strike on Tuesday, demanding a 14 percent increase in wages and a 70 percent rise in holiday pay.
The early morning strike followed two one-hour stoppages at the end of April. Only international trains, which are protected by Slovenian law, are running to schedule.

"Our last talk with the management on Monday brought no result as they insist on their offer of a three percent pay increase only," Slavko Kmetic, head of the association of railway unions, told Reuters.

He said the avarage gross monthly salary of a railway worker in February was 128,000 tolars ($819), well below the average Slovenian salary of 136,800 tolars, while last year's holiday pay amounted to 74,000 tolars.

But the management reiterated it could not agree to the demands because of the poor financial situation of the state-owned railways, which posted a loss of 3.6 billion tolars in 1996, down from a profit of 68 million in 1995.
The company said the main reason for the loss was a decline in cargo traffic, which had suffered from high administrative costs.
"The loss is the concern of the government which does not invest sufficiently in the railway infrastructure," Kmetic said.
He said negotiations were expected to continue on Friday but added that another four-hour strike would be staged on May 13 if talks had not yielded any result by then.
This is the first major stoppage to be held this year, after a series of strikes dogged the government before a general election in November 1996.
